label: Week 34, 2026
recap:
This week's US AI policy activity was modest, centered mainly on California, which accounted for 4 of the tracked items, alongside 2 from the United States Congress. Legislative attention touched on government use, with 2 bills, and transparency and disclosure, with 2 bills, including California SB1159. Smaller threads appeared in consumer protection and discrimination, with 1 bill from the United States Congress, HB10110, elections, with 1 bill, and health care, with 1 bill, California SB1133. Three bills tracked this week did not fall under a specific theme. There were 6 bill movements, meaning records changed status, not that any bill passed.

On the agency side, activity was limited to 2 federal documents, tied to the Civil Rights Commission and the Commerce Department, one mention each. Litigation was the busier side of the week, with 13 case updates recorded, though no details on individual cases are available here. Overall, this was a quiet week, with a small, spread out set of legislative themes and a somewhat heavier flow of case activity, covering the period from August 17 to August 23, 2026.

federal.title: Solicitation of Nominations for Membership on the NOAA Science Advisory Board (SAB)
federal.detail: The NOAA Science Advisory Board (SAB) is the only Federal Advisory Committee with responsibility to advise the Under Secretary of Commerce for Oceans and Atmosphere on long- and short-range strategies for research, education and the application of science to resource management and environmental assessment and prediction. NOAA seeks candidates with expertise in areas relevant to its mission, including Federal, State, and local government; social and behavioral sciences; artificial intelligence and machine learning; high performance computing; data management, including open access and accessibility; uncrewed systems; whale research and conservation; aircraft systems and modernization; and economic analysis, including cost-benefit evaluation of observing systems. NOAA also encourages nominations of qualified mid-career scientists and engineers.
